The invitation came through Torhh, who approached Senareth at the water's edge where they still sometimes worked patterns together.

The mountain at the island's center had always been the Tidecallers' territory—the place they retreated to when fear overwhelmed curiosity, where they maintained their largest population concentration.

Senareth brought only a small group—Elyraen for their analytical precision, Vairis for practical engineering sense, Olythae for artistic vision, and Kyreth whose gentle nature had first broken through Torhh's fear.
Water channels threaded through the mountain—not for drinking, but for music.

The Tidecallers directed underground streams through carved passages that made the entire structure sing when tide changed, when rain fell, when ocean currents shifted in the waters surrounding the island.
The Tidecaller mountain became legend among the other Giant factions—proof that cooperation between species could create beauty beyond what either achieved alone.
